# CoreWeave's CFO says contract prices rose 25% in July

How tight GPU compute is shows up in contract prices; public list-price indexes can't read it. CoreWeave, a cloud provider that specializes in renting out GPUs, had its CFO say on the August 11 earnings call that prices rose about 25% across all models in July. getdeploying, a public index that compiles list prices from dozens of providers' websites, showed only a 5% rise over the year at the time. A one-time price increase and a full-year cumulative rise cover different periods, and the two numbers don't measure the same kind of price.

CoreWeave's second-quarter report shows 98% of revenue came from committed contracts that are paid whether used or not, with pay-as-you-go at only about 2%. CoreWeave's website price for H100, US$6.16 per GPU-hour, is exactly the price the index picks up. The 25% most likely landed on newly signed and renewed contracts; that is the deep dive's reading from the quarterly report and the website, and the CFO didn't say which price it applied to. After other providers raised list prices in October, the index's one-year rise climbed to 18%.

Reading only a public list-price index to judge whether AI compute is in surplus makes the market look looser than it is; what matters is how fast new contract prices pull up the average across all contracts. The next check is CoreWeave's third-quarter results in November. SecondSource's October 26 issue, "B200 deals top Nebius list price; only Ornn's index shows it," reported that one index provider had measured transaction prices above list, pointing the same way (full deep dive).
